name: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents (Zhang et al.)
venue: ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS); accepted 2025-07-02 (DOI 10.1145/3748302). First released as arXiv:2404.13501 [cs.AI] on 2024-04-21. The task label 'ACM TOIS 2024' refers to the same TOIS publication; the arXiv preprint is dated 2024 and the journal acceptance is 2025.
authors_affiliation: Zeyu Zhang, Xiaohe Bo, Chen Ma, Rui Li, Xu Chen (corresponding), Ji-Rong Wen — Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China, Beijing; Quanyu Dai, Jieming Zhu, Zhenhua Dong — Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, China.
code_url: N/A (a survey; no method code. A curated paper-list repository is maintained instead.)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/nuster1128/LLM_Agent_Memory_Survey (curated paper list, ~495 stars; README last updated 2025-07-27; tracks works on memory sources/forms/operations/evaluation/applications).
task_domain: Survey/taxonomy of the memory mechanism of LLM-based agents, spanning conversation, role-playing/social simulation, multi-source QA, long-context applications, recommendation, code generation, embodied/open-world (e.g., Minecraft via Voyager/GITM), and decision-making agents (anchor memory survey, not a single task method).
problem_setting: A holistic survey that defines what agent memory is and why it is needed (cognitive psychology, self-evolution, applications), then systematically reviews HOW memory is designed and evaluated for LLM-based agents. Settings covered are predominantly interactive and long-horizon agent-environment loops (single- and multi-agent), where memory enables self-evolution via experience accumulation, environment exploration, and knowledge abstraction. Supervision varies by surveyed work; the survey itself proposes no new method, dataset, or experiments and offers a unified framework abstracting common design patterns. It explicitly notes that, at the time, there were no open-sourced benchmarks tailored specifically for evaluating agent memory modules.
what_is_retrieved: Across surveyed systems: experiences / trajectories (inside-trial and cross-trial information), summaries/insights, external knowledge (docs/KB/APIs), and dialogue/episodic records. The survey frames retrieval as the 'memory reading' operation that pulls relevant stored memory entries (raw histories, summaries, retrieved memory pieces, external knowledge) for the current state.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID — the survey's memory-sources taxonomy spans inside-trial information and cross-trial information (a GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes during interaction) plus External Knowledge (a STATIC external corpus such as docs/KB). It explicitly distinguishes dynamically generated in-loop memory from static out-of-loop external knowledge.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Survey-level: reviewed memory-reading methods predominantly use fixed top-k similarity retrieval (e.g., ExpeL retrieves top-K most-similar successful trajectories via FAISS); the survey does not advocate a single completeness-vs-top-k objective. It treats retrieval as relevance-driven reading and does not frame a minimal-set completeness goal.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (a survey, not a CBR method). However, the surveyed memory-operation framework (Writing / Management / Reading) plus experience-accumulation maps loosely onto CBR's Retain/Revise/Retrieve, though the survey does not use CBR phase terminology.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False — the survey frames memory via cognitive psychology (sensory/short-term/long-term memory analogies) and a sources/forms/operations taxonomy; it does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: Survey taxonomy of memory units rather than one unit: inside-trial steps (observations, thoughts, actions), cross-trial trajectories/experiences, distilled summaries/insights, dialogue segments (topic-keyed), structured relations (e.g., entity relations in TiM), and external knowledge documents. Retrieved 'reading' units are memory entries at these granularities (full trajectory / sub-trajectory / summary / document).
index_source: Hybrid construction. Memory store is built from (a) dynamically generated in-loop information (inside-trial and cross-trial, written online during agent-environment interaction) and (b) static external knowledge induced offline. The survey explicitly contrasts dynamically generated memory with static external information.
index_structure_topology: Surveyed stores span multiple topologies: flat vector index (e.g., ExpeL using FAISS), structured/relational database (ChatDB SQL, TiM structured relation DB grouping similar contents), topic-keyed segment indices (MemoChat), hierarchical/virtual-context memory (MemGPT), and parametric stores (encoded into model parameters). No single topology is prescribed; the survey organizes by source/form/operation rather than index topology.
retriever_type: Survey-level: surveyed memory-reading methods use mainly text-similarity dense retrieval (e.g., ExpeL FAISS top-K similarity), LLM-generated query/SQL retrieval (ChatDB Chain-of-Memory SQL), and rule/agent-directed reading; for parametric memory, 'reading' is implicit forward-pass use of encoded parameters. Hybrid across works; no canonical retriever is proposed.
retriever_learning_signal: Survey-level: most reviewed reading mechanisms are off-the-shelf (text similarity, auxiliary scoring such as recency/relevance/importance as in Generative Agents). Some are LM-/agent-directed (LLM generates SQL or decides what to read). The survey does not propose a learned retriever; learning signals discussed are mainly heuristic relevance/recency/importance rather than trained ranking models.
query_construction: Survey-level: queries to memory are formed from the current state/task (raw current query), agent-generated structured queries (ChatDB generates SQL as a Chain-of-Memory in advance), and Chain-of-Thought-guided selection (MPC provides CoT examples to ignore certain memory). Construction is method-dependent; the survey abstracts it as state-conditioned memory reading.
query_granularity: Survey-level: predominantly step/state-level reading (memory is read for the current state during reasoning/decision-making), with task-level reads also present; the survey does not standardize a query granularity.
when_to_retrieve: Survey-level: both one-shot and iterative reading appear across surveyed works; memory reading is invoked when the agent needs information for reasoning/decision-making (often per step/turn). Some works use a controller to decide when to operate on memory (e.g., SCM memory controller). No single trigger policy is prescribed.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Survey-level: triggers across works include fixed schedule (read each step/turn), agent-initiated/self-directed access (MemGPT self-directed memory ops; ChatDB agent-generated SQL reads), and controller-decided operations (SCM memory controller deciding when to write/manage/read). The survey does not adopt token-confidence or attention-based triggers as a unifying signal.
reranking: Survey-level: not a focus; surveyed reading typically uses top-K by similarity plus auxiliary scoring (relevance, recency, importance, e.g., Generative Agents' retrieval scoring) rather than a dedicated cross-encoder reranking stage. No standardized reranker is proposed.
retrieved_context_refinement: Survey-level: refinement is treated under 'Memory Management' (reflection, summarization, abstraction, merging of stored entries) and at write time (storing summaries/insights vs raw info). At read time most works do similarity top-K with light auxiliary scoring. Distractor filtering/compression are discussed mainly as management/summarization, not as a separate post-retrieval module.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (memory survey; tool/skill-description engineering is out of scope, though external-knowledge and skill-library memory such as Voyager's skill code are mentioned).
index_content_separation: Partially covered: hierarchical/virtual-context memory (e.g., MemGPT) separates a small in-context working memory from a larger external store paged in on demand; topic-keyed indexing (MemoChat) stores topic keys for indexing fuller memory pieces. The survey discusses this as a memory-management/forms pattern rather than a formal index-vs-content separation principle.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / integration protocol; memory stores grow via in-loop writing rather than tool-API CRUD sync).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (inter-tool dependency modeling is out of scope for this memory survey).
how_retrieved_used: Survey-level: retrieved memory is used as prompt augmentation (injecting recalled context/experiences into the LLM prompt for reasoning and decision-making), as experience reuse for self-evolution, and—in parametric form—as a training signal/parameter encoding that implicitly influences actions (fine-tuning, model editing). The survey frames usage as providing information for LLM inference via the reading operation.
planning_integration: Survey-level: memory supports planning/acting by supplying past experiences/observations at plan and act time (e.g., Reflexion/ExpeL reuse cross-trial reflections; Voyager/GITM use skill/experience memory for open-world planning). The survey abstracts this as memory enabling experience accumulation, exploration guidance, and knowledge abstraction rather than prescribing a specific plan-time integration.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Survey-level: reviewed works interleave memory reading at per-turn / per-step granularity during reasoning and decision-making; the survey does not impose a single interleaving granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (a survey, not a CBR adaptation method). Surveyed 'memory management' (reflection/abstraction/summarization) and write-time summarization are the closest analogues to case revision/adaptation.
retrieved_item_representation: Survey-level: two top-level forms — Textual form (raw histories, recent/complete context, retrieved memory pieces, summaries/insights, external knowledge as natural language) and Parametric form (memory encoded into model parameters via fine-tuning or model editing, latent/soft representation). Surface forms thus range from raw trajectory to distilled summary to structured relation to latent parameters.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Survey-level spectrum: raw inside-trial steps/observations, cross-trial trajectories, distilled summaries/insights/abstracted knowledge (knowledge abstraction), and structured relations. The survey explicitly highlights moving from raw observations to higher-level abstracted concepts as a key memory function.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Survey-level: discussed via write-time information extraction/summarization (original info is 'lengthy and noisy', so extraction strategy is vital), memory management (reflection/merging to consolidate), and CoT-guided ignoring of irrelevant memory (MPC). No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT is proposed by the survey itself.
memory_type: Survey/taxonomy — covers all listed types: episodic (in-loop dialogue/observation histories), skill-library (e.g., Voyager skills), workflow/procedural experiences, structured/graph-like relational memory (TiM), and latent/parametric memory (fine-tuning, model editing). It does not pick one; it taxonomizes textual vs parametric forms over inside-trial/cross-trial/external sources.
write_back: True (survey-level) — 'Memory Writing' is one of the three core operations: agents store perceived information (raw and/or summarized) for future use; many surveyed systems (MemGPT, MemoChat, TiM, Reflexion/ExpeL) write back experiences/summaries. The survey describes write-back as central, not a single implementation.
online_growth: Yes (survey-level) — inside-trial and cross-trial memory grow dynamically during agent-environment interaction (written online), while external-knowledge memory may be static. The survey explicitly distinguishes dynamically generated in-loop memory from static out-of-loop information.
write_back_trigger: Survey-level: triggers vary across works — self-directed/autonomous writing (MemGPT updates memory based on context), controller-decided writing (SCM memory controller decides when to execute operations), per-segment summarization (MemoChat summarizes each conversation segment), and reflective writing after trials (Reflexion/ExpeL store reflections/experiences). The survey notes designing the information-extraction (write) strategy is vital but prescribes no single trigger.
failure_experience_usage: Survey-level: explicitly highlighted — a key memory function is to remember past error plannings, inappropriate behaviors, and failed experiences so the agent handles similar future tasks better (self-evolution via experience accumulation). Surveyed systems (e.g., Reflexion/Retroformer/ExpeL) store both successful and failed/negative trial experiences for reuse.
memory_evolution_update: Survey-level: covered under 'Memory Management' — stored entries can be processed/abstracted over time via reflection, summarization/abstraction, and merging of similar contents (e.g., TiM groups similar contents; reflection/merging consolidate memory). So beyond append-only, dedup-merge and refine/abstract dynamics are surveyed; the survey notes parametric memory needs no manual merging rules unlike textual memory.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No (survey-level) — reviewed memory reading is predominantly fixed similarity top-K plus heuristic relevance/recency/importance scoring or agent-generated queries; the survey does not center RL/learned retrieval policies (it precedes much of the M-MDP/RL-retrieval line), and proposes no learned policy itself.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Survey-level: largely single-agent private memory, but the survey explicitly flags 'Memory in LLM-based Multi-agent Applications' as a future direction (memory shared/coordinated across agents, e.g., MetaGPT/ChatDev multi-agent settings) and reviews multi-agent systems where memory is exchanged. Cross-framework shared experience is identified as an open direction rather than a solved mechanism.
benchmarks: No new benchmark is introduced. The survey reviews indirect-evaluation tasks/datasets used by other works (conversation, multi-source question-answering, long-context applications, and other tasks) and direct-evaluation question sets constructed from agent histories. It explicitly states there are no open-sourced benchmarks tailored for LLM-agent memory modules. Surveyed open-world/embodied settings include Minecraft (Voyager, GITM).
benchmark_family: memory (agent-memory evaluation survey) — primarily QA / conversation / long-context / multi-source-QA task families used for indirect memory evaluation, plus embodied/open-world (Minecraft) among reviewed applications. Predates dedicated memory benchmarks like LoCoMo/LongMemEval.
baselines: N/A — a survey with no experiments; it compares and tabulates representative memory systems (MemoryBank, RET-LLM, ChatDB, TiM, SCM, Voyager, MemGPT, MemoChat, MPC, Generative Agents, RecMind, Retroformer, ExpeL, Synapse, GITM, ReAct, Reflexion, RecAgent, Character-LLM, MetaGPT, ChatDev, etc.) along the sources/forms/operations axes (Tables 1-3) rather than benchmarking baselines.
key_metrics: Survey-level taxonomy of evaluation metrics. Direct: subjective (Coherence, Rationality via human/GPT-4 judgment) and objective (Result Correctness = accuracy of memory-based answers; Reference Accuracy = whether the retrieved/recalled memory matches ground-truth references; plus efficiency metrics). Indirect: task-completion metrics for conversation (consistency, engagement), multi-source QA accuracy, long-context performance, etc.
headline_result: N/A (no empirical headline number; it is a survey). Its headline contribution is a unified framework: a memory taxonomy along Sources (inside-trial / cross-trial / external knowledge), Forms (textual vs parametric), and Operations (writing / management / reading), plus a Direct vs Indirect evaluation framework.
ablations: N/A (no experiments/ablations). The survey's comparative tables (Table 1 memory sources, Table 2 memory forms, Table 3 memory operations) function as a structured cross-system comparison clarifying which design choices each system adopts.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes (conceptually) — the survey's central evaluation contribution is exactly this decoupling: Direct Evaluation measures the memory module as a stand-alone component (intrinsic: coherence/rationality, result correctness, reference accuracy) separately from Indirect Evaluation via end-to-end agent task success. It argues direct evaluation improves reliability since task performance conflates many factors.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, as a taxonomy: outcome metrics via indirect end-to-end task completion; process/intermediate metrics via direct evaluation (Reference Accuracy targets the intermediate recalled-memory quality, not just the final answer; coherence/rationality assess recalled-memory quality). The survey advocates measuring intermediate memory quality, not only final outcome.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively: textual memory is interpretable and easy to expand/edit but less storage- and efficiency-optimal; parametric memory is more storage-efficient (knowledge compression) and robust but harder to edit/interpret. Objective evaluation is noted to include efficiency metrics. No concrete latency/cost numbers (it is a survey).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Survey-level: context-window limits are a core motivation (long-horizon interactions exceed context budget, motivating external memory + reading top-K). Hierarchical/virtual-context memory (MemGPT) manages a bounded in-context budget by paging memory; reads are typically fixed top-K by similarity. No single budget/k value is prescribed.
survey_scope_and_axes: Organizing axes: (Why) cognitive psychology / self-evolution / applications; (How to design) Memory Sources {inside-trial, cross-trial, external knowledge} x Memory Forms {textual: complete/recent/retrieved/external; parametric: fine-tuning, model editing} x Memory Operations {writing, management, reading}; (How to evaluate) Direct {subjective: coherence, rationality; objective: result correctness, reference accuracy} vs Indirect {conversation, multi-source QA, long-context, other}; plus memory-enhanced applications and future directions (parametric memory, multi-agent memory, lifelong learning, humanoid agents). ~174 references; coverage window through early 2024 (v1, April 2024).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (proposes no benchmark). It notably observes the absence of open-sourced benchmarks dedicated to LLM-agent memory at the time, and reviews how others construct direct-evaluation questions from agent histories with annotated ground-truth answers/references.
builds_on: Cognitive-psychology memory theory (sensory/short-term/long-term memory) as an organizing analogy; foundational LLM-agent and memory systems it taxonomizes — Generative Agents (memory stream with recency/relevance/importance), MemGPT (virtual context management), Reflexion / Retroformer (verbal reflection memory), ExpeL (experiential learning, FAISS trajectory retrieval), Voyager / GITM (skill/experience memory for open-world agents), MemoryBank, RET-LLM, ChatDB, TiM, SCM, MemoChat, MPC, RecAgent.
contrasts_with: Positions itself against prior surveys that treated LLM-agent memory only in passing or in scattered papers without a holistic source/form/operation framework, and against general LLM-agent surveys (e.g., Wang et al. agent survey, Xi et al.) that do not center memory. It contrasts textual vs parametric memory forms and direct vs indirect evaluation as design dichotomies.
lineage: Surveys group — an anchor/foundational memory survey for LLM-based agents. It sits upstream of later, more granular memory and experience surveys (e.g., 2026 'From Storage to Experience', 'Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents') and underpins the experience/case-memory planner lineage by formalizing sources (inside/cross-trial/external), textual-vs-parametric forms, and the writing/management/reading operation cycle plus direct/indirect evaluation.
